name: Clifford ledger: UK AI policy connection map
headline: A hand-checked record of 73 source documents, 54 dated events and 286 person-to-event entries yields about 93 documented links among 170 people; it shows Matt Clifford held Faculty shares (declared 10 Oct 2024) while Marc Warner and Saul Klein were Faculty directors, that the only Starmer-Clifford link is the 13 Jan 2025 Action Plan response, and that no document puts Clifford and any Anduril person on one instrument.
rows: The Clifford ledger: who shared a documented room with Matt Clifford (UK AI policy map)
Cross-corpus public-interest map (inventory of all lanes)
Reported-link upgrade check
Big-institution guard review
note: All 95 evidence bases are official records or primary statements (none press-only); names ~170 real people, so keep the 'shared room is not a relationship' wording prominent and get one outside reader.

name: Matt Clifford and Anduril: a documented non-link
headline: Clifford led the AI Opportunities Action Plan (50 recommendations, 13 Jan 2025), was made an unpaid adviser the same day and published his interests on 24 Feb 2025; the only Anduril overlap is attendance at separate AI Safety Summit sessions, and Anduril's UK TALOS contract predates his roles, so no joint meeting, deal or procurement effect was found.
rows: Matt Clifford: AI adviser role and any Anduril link
note: A careful negative about a living public figure the repo is named after; who selected him and how conflicts were handled in decisions remain unknown.

name: Electric Twin ownership and the Atomico round
headline: Eleven Companies House filings show Electric Twin raised $14M ($4M pre-seed, then a $10M round led by Atomico in Feb 2026, with LocalGlobe, Mercuri, Samos and Marc Andreessen; angels include Palantir UK's Louis Mosley); at 27 Sep 2025 Atomico vehicles held 604,294 Seed 2 shares, LocalGlobe 631,578 Seed 1 plus 48,559 Seed 2, founders Cooper and Warner 1,000,000 ordinary shares each, and Atomico's Benjamin Blume joined the board on 12 Sep 2025.
rows: Electric Twin: who owns it, and who bought the September 2025 shares
Electric Twin capital, board control and the unfinished register-of-members bridge
note: Filings cannot prove who bought which tranche; the drafted Companies Act s.116 register request was never sent and the ~7 PRs of 'reply-processing' tooling for it can go. 2026 SH01 capture sits on branch diagnostic/electric-twin-2026-sh01-form-custody-v2.

name: Electric Twin's '96% independently validated' claim
headline: The '96% accurate, independently validated by LSE' claim traces to SSRN working paper 6439338 (7,755 UK respondents) whose own disclosures say the evaluator is Electric Twin's science adviser and shareholder, a co-author is a co-founder and Electric Twin funded the study; the OSF registration is exploratory with no replication package, the 95.5% 1-MAE and 92% NDAM figures rest on a private benchmark, and the homepage's '155 countries' claim is backed by validation covering the UK and US only.
rows: Electric Twin 'independent validation' claim, capability lineage and the Gartner roster
Metric and benchmark governance for synthetic audiences (1-MAE / NDAM reproducibility)
Cross-cultural / multilingual extrapolation of synthetic audiences
note: Lives only in closed issue comments (bulk-closed 11 Aug 2026); role overlap is a governance fact, not evidence of bad science, and the derived NDAM equation must not be quoted as the vendor's definition. Re-fetch sources into main before use.

name: Synthetic audiences in real use: Times ExplorAItion and others
headline: News UK and Electric Twin both confirm that Times ExplorAItion (launched 27 Apr 2026) runs AI 'synthetic audiences' built from subscriber behaviour, reader panels and PAMCo data for campaign planning, message pre-testing and targeting; the publisher says human research stays the gold standard, data-controller roles and retention are unspecified, Aaru told Semafor it was hired by campaigns and super PACs (no FEC trace found), and a Cabinet Office disclosure records a 2 Apr 2025 Electric Twin meeting on 'AI capability'.
rows: Real synthetic-audience deployments (News UK Times ExplorAItion and others)
Publisher synthetic-audience deployments (Times ExplorAItion, Dentsu, PAMCo)
Political message-optimisation and defence/government deployment of synthetic audiences
note: No evidence of manipulation was found or inferable; the drafted request to News UK for one paired example was never sent. PAMCo and rate-card context is in closed issue #39 only.

name: Faculty to Accenture: the dated transaction
headline: Accenture announced its agreement to take over Faculty on 6 Jan 2026 and completion on 16 Mar 2026, Companies House records Accenture Plc as person with significant control of Faculty Science Ltd (08873131) from 12 Mar 2026, more than 400 staff moved and Marc Warner became an Accenture CTO while staying Faculty CEO.
rows: Faculty to Accenture: transaction control and capability transfer
note: Small but register-backed; main holds 24 Faculty Science Ltd files but not this transaction, and it is one hop from the Clifford-Faculty shareholding in the ledger.

name: Clinical-trial 'digital twins': what the EMA actually qualified
headline: The EMA's CHMP qualified only PROCOVA's linear prognostic-score adjustment for randomized trials with continuous outcomes and explicitly did not qualify the machine-learning model-building step; the FDA's ISTAND list showed zero qualified tools on 1 Jan 2026, and the one named human use (REM127 trial NCT05478031) kept an ordinary placebo arm and was terminated for liver signals.
rows: Clinical-trial digital twins: what EMA actually qualified (PROCOVA / Unlearn)
note: Seven EMA PDFs fetched and SHA-256 hashed, nine stakeholder comments read; exists only in closed-issue comments, so re-capture into main.

name: Palantir: how much is government, who controls it
headline: Palantir's 2025 annual report shows $2.402B of government revenue (54% of total; US government $1.9B, up from $1.2B in 2024), founders can control up to roughly 50% of votes, the government owns its data while Palantir keeps platform IP, and 2026 shareholder proposals to curb founder voting were defeated, so the 'hidden control' claim fails because SEC filings disclose it.
rows: Palantir: government revenue, founder control and dependency
note: Award-level profit and any personal enrichment are not shown.

name: Army DCGS-A: the outside check that worked
headline: In the Army's intelligence-software program a Federal Circuit ruling (Palantir v. United States, 2018) forced a commercial-market review without ordering Palantir chosen, GAO then denied both Palantir's (B-412746) and General Dynamics' (B-416181) protests, the re-competition drew 8 proposals and 2 awards, and the Army reported 879 systems fielded to 402 battalions by FY2021.
rows: DCGS-A (Army intelligence software): was Palantir locked in?
Palantir DCGS-A2 procurement challenge
SSC residual-denominator Wave 03: lanes left open (RD-06-C04 Capability Drop evaluation closure)
note: Only 3 of 8 bidders are public, so 'foreclosure' and 'technical superiority' are not established; the RD-06-C04 lane seed on the other 5 was never run.

name: Army NGC2: not a closed Anduril-Palantir duo
headline: In the Army's Next Generation Command and Control program Anduril leads the 4th Infantry Division stack with Palantir's Foundry and Raft's registries as components, Lockheed Martin leads a separate 25th Infantry Division version, and more than 80 proposals were received, so the program is multi-vendor even though the rejected-vendor record and any human override logs are not public.
rows: Army NGC2: Anduril, Palantir and who really controls it
note: Whether the shared data layer can be swapped out is untested.

name: Leaving Palantir: Homes for Ukraine and the NHS
headline: UK Homes for Ukraine moved from a Palantir Foundry-supported service to an in-house system called Share with three years of data migrated and public code; the NHS COVID-19 data store ran on Foundry, the 2023 Federated Data Platform tender (seven bids) said it would replace it yet retained Palantir, NHS England paid Palantir a separate 12-month GBP 24.925m transition-and-exit contract, and DHSC paid Mozaic GBP 100,000 in 2021 to move the Adult Social Care Dashboard off Foundry.
rows: Can a government exit a vendor like Palantir?
Pandemic decision infrastructure to NHS Federated Data Platform
M-04D Wave 09: practical exit and substitution in UK health Palantir lanes
note: No independent audit of HFU deletion or cost savings; the NHS wave-09 verdicts (9 Contracts Finder sources) sit on branch agent/m04d-fog-resolution-wave-09 one file away from waves 01-08 on main; the pandemic-to-FDP chain is in closed issue #34.

name: Does public money come back? TARP versus defence and chips
headline: Only the 2008 bank bailout closes the loop: TARP paid out $204.9B and ended with $16.3B net income (M&I Bank alone returned $1.9448B on $1.715B), whereas the NATO Innovation Fund, UK NSSIF, the CHIPS deals (Polar Semiconductor upside-sharing, I-Pulse stake) and NASA COTS have rights on paper but no realised public return yet.
rows: Does public defense and chip money come back to the public?
note: Honest 'not yet' for every defence case; nothing reaches affected people.

name: The government's Intel stake: no cash yet
headline: As of 4 Sep 2026 Commerce held 274,583,000 Intel shares plus a warrant for up to 240.5M at $20 in exchange for $8.87B of subsidies, about 16M escrowed shares were released and about 143M still held back, no sale, dividend, warrant exercise or cash receipt appears in SEC filings, and Intel's Aug 2026 210.5M-share offering was Intel selling, not the government.
rows: Has the US government cashed in its Intel stake?
Intel CHIPS equity: did the government holder realize value? (held-evidence packets)
note: Re-runnable null with hash-bound receipts; a branch packet shows a shared SEC registration number (333-292925) cannot identify a seller. 21 data files and ~20 workflows for one 'not yet' is heavy; fold into one monitor.

name: Erebor bank: regulator records and a non-network investor
headline: Regulator records show OCC conditional charter approval with a capital floor, FDIC approval and an opening on 6 Feb 2026 for the Luckey-linked bank, and a Fundrise fund bought $5M of Erebor Series B stock on 20 Feb 2026, which rules out the idea that only the defence-tech network funded it.
rows: Erebor bank and Silent Ventures money trail
note: Other round participants, board and veto rights, Silent Ventures' real investors and customer traffic remain unknown.

name: Pentagon strategic-capital loans: one of five executed
headline: The Office of Strategic Capital received 200+ applications asking $8.9B against $984M of initial capacity; of five named instruments totalling $2.075B only MP Materials' $150M 12-year unsecured 5.38% note has actually closed, while Vulcan Elements $620M, ReElement $80M, Phoenix Tailings $500M and Energy Fuels $725M are conditional commitments with no closing, draw or repayment seen.
rows: Office of Strategic Capital: who got the money, on what terms?
Pentagon strategic capital: OSC loans, SBIC funds and the space advisory committee
note: Only 8 of 70 term fields were observable (15 official routes returned 403); no favoritism finding. Row 40 also summarises SBIC and ACES, inventoried separately.

name: X-Bow: press figures versus the federal spending record
headline: For X-Bow's rocket-motor factory contract (FA9300-25-C-6015, 25 Sep 2025) the Pentagon announcement says $191.3M total with $121.5M committed from foreign-military-sales money ending April 2029, while USAspending shows $129.5M committed, $199.3M potential, July 2028 completion, no foreign funding and one transaction; none of five ranked startups' press-reported award figures matched official records exactly.
rows: NatSec100 award check and the X-Bow contract mismatch
note: No wrongdoing claimed and no cause for the $8M gap found; a repeatable method.

name: California food-benefit appeals: 12,282 decisions, no proof of restoration
headline: The entire FY2025-26 California CalFresh hearing registry (12,282 decisions, 11,672 PDFs) shows 4,229 denials, 1,418 dismissals and roughly 6,633 outcomes with some relief (1,190 grants, 2,479 partial, 2,964 settlements), yet a search for public proof that counties actually restored benefits in those ~6,300 cases found zero receipts.
rows: California CalFresh: do hearings actually give benefits back?
note: The ~54% figure is arithmetic on the registry, which the repo itself refuses to label a finding; ~1,433 decision PDFs with text sit in a 226MB archive in the repo and 11,672 in a draft release - check redaction before sharing anything but the table.

name: Core thesis and its stress test against public records
headline: The project's big idea (governments handing strategy and delivery to private firms until they are hard to remove) was attacked in seven rounds producing 63 narrow rulings: 42 supported for human review, 5 non-links, 8 unproven, none disproved; supported items include GAO's at least $33.9B over ~57,000 Iraq/Afghanistan contracts after 1990s staff cuts, while 'one founder network runs it all' and 'hidden Palantir control' were not supported.
rows: Core thesis: how public capacity turns into private infrastructure, then power
Stress test of the core thesis (Palantir, Anduril, ICE, Army, Ukraine, Erebor bank)
note: All rulings are maintainer-plus-AI; 'supported for human review' is not 'proven'.

name: Answerable power: the seven-part check, seen separately never together
headline: Every ingredient of a real check on a powerful system has been found somewhere - a pre-action stay (Idaho K.W. v. Armstrong), a banned system (Dutch SyRI), a public replacement (Homes for Ukraine), a binding worker veto (German works councils, BAG 1 ABR 7/15) and money returned (TARP) - but no case has all of them, so the project's own test is not met.
rows: Answerable power: is there a working check on power asymmetry?
note: 68 official sources; the intellectual core of the project and the frame the A-tier exit and value-return findings hang on.

name: Who acts on a hunch and who must prove harm (epistemic jurisdiction)
headline: Fifteen systems (Palantir/Army/ICE/NHS/Brave1 plus Post Office Horizon, COMPAS, Idaho Medicaid, SyRI, Robodebt, student-visa terminations) run through eight tests give 122 records from 66 sources, with the burden-of-proof asymmetry firmest where courts or inquiries forced the record (Horizon, Robodebt) and a single cross-system pattern explicitly not promoted.
rows: Epistemic jurisdiction: who sets the threshold and who must prove harm
Who may act on a hunch and who must prove injury afterward (epistemic jurisdiction)
note: Most transferable idea in the pile; rulings are maintainer-only.

name: ICE ImmigrationOS to one arrest in Woodburn, Oregon
headline: A chain from Executive Order 14159 through the Palantir-built ImmigrationOS contract to ICE workflows is supported, and for the 30 Oct 2025 Woodburn operation a Palantir-attributed ELITE app helped pick the target area before separate plate checks, a van stop, an arrest and release after a habeas filing; ELITE did not identify the individual and Palantir was not shown to be the sole cause.
rows: ICE ImmigrationOS, case tools and the Woodburn arrests
note: Rare person-level chain with non-links stated, but the ELITE attribution needs a second source.

name: Anduril access-and-ownership brief
headline: A sequenced packet of 21 dated events, 24 claims (15 verified, 9 needing review) and 22 records - Q2 2025 Senate lobbying filing, FEC PAC data, the Area-I, Adranos and Numerica acquisitions, a rocket-motor award, CBP and Army contracts, GAO denying Anduril's 2021 protest and a competitively bid $642M Marine Corps contract with ten offers - that draws no causal conclusion.
rows: Anduril: access, ownership and the government gate (reporter brief)
Public reporter briefs (Anduril; Arcadia, California)
US defence estate (Anduril, Swarm Forge contests, defence-tech people)
Public money into defense firms: Anduril awards and a CHIPS control
note: Most reader-ready piece; finish the 9 unverified claims and drop the separate 'merit circularity' framing (DPA $14.3M award vs company's $43.7M claim) which was ruled unsupported. Row 85 also covers the Arcadia brief.

name: Arcadia, California: testing a chatbot's 'master plan' against records
headline: Of 19 claims about downtown Arcadia's land, water, rail and transit, 7 were confirmed, 4 corrected and 5 unresolved from 142 receipts; a side branch adds deed data (the Alexan Azalea block bought 24 Jan 2018 for $25.6M) and shows the Downtown Arcadia Improvement Association is a 2013 nonprofit with FY2025 revenue of $160,121, not a city-created district, while the claimed '1993 Downtown Revitalization Strategy' was never found.
rows: Arcadia, California field autopsy (a chatbot's 'master plan' claim)
Local development estate (Arcadia CA plus place-formation tracks)
Arcadia field autopsy - second research increment (seven trails closed on a side branch)
Place-formation controls: Azusa, Duarte, Monrovia Gold Line districts
note: Branch claude/arcadia-field-autopsy-xqrkkn closes 7 of 10 open trails but is 2,423 commits behind main; 33 Azusa/Duarte/Monrovia control issues never started.

name: Opportunity Zones: was money already in place before the 2018 map?
headline: SEC Form D shows zero 'qualified opportunity fund' filings before the 14 Jun 2018 designation (first on 21 Jun 2018), while Maryland deed records show the Port Covington assemblage was bought in 2014-2016 ($46.5M on 23 Dec 2014; a July 2016 cluster summing to the $70.3M the Baltimore Sun reported) before Governor Hogan selected the tract, alongside four other press-documented cases of already-owned land placed in zones.
rows: Opportunity Zones: was money already in place before the 2018 designation?
note: Fund-route null and Port Covington deeds are primary; but the Detroit and Nevada quotes are marked unverified in receipts while the dossier says verified, deeds redact owner names so the Plank link rests on press, and the README still says 'scaffold'. Reconcile labels and archive sources.

name: Synthetic-audience market map (F-01 to F-20)
headline: A 77-source screen of the market around AI 'synthetic audiences' found seven anchored rows (CACI Fresco and Verve VIPS, Principality Building Society and Verve, News UK and Electric Twin, MRS/ESOMAR/AAPOR rules, EMA/Unlearn) and four ad-holding-company operating systems (WPP Open/InfoSum, Dentsu.Connect/Evidenza, Publicis CoreAI/Epsilon, Omnicom Omni/Acxiom) already able to admit a simulated audience, with no public joined campaign receipt; the Gartner list of 33 vendors was never obtained (14 recovered from vendors' own posts).
rows: Second-order frontier seams of the synthetic-population market (F-01..F-20)
Gartner's list of 33 synthetic-audience vendors
UK state-market estate (synthetic-population thesis)
Synthetic populations: are AI-modelled publics becoming decision infrastructure?
note: 67 of 77 locators are absent from main; the thesis kernel on main has 2 of 16 cases started (a former No.10 adviser's consultancy conditions; 10DS/i.AI/GDS lineage). Speculative market-structure claims need the comments' 'no inference' boundaries kept.

name: What synthetic-audience vendors disclose about models, clouds and data
headline: Electric Twin names no model, cloud or subprocessor; Verve claims API-only private instances but names no provider; Yabble discloses OpenAI plus AWS and warns it does not scrub personal data; Aaru publishes a processor-role DPA; Times ExplorAItion inputs are said to involve 'no personal data' but controller/processor roles, lawful basis and retention are not public, and ICO guidance says pseudonymised data stays personal.
rows: Foundation-model, cloud and subprocessor dependence of synthetic-audience vendors
Synthetic-data lineage, consent and anonymisation
note: Vendor self-statements 2023-2025 and policy-page readings, not legal advice or audit.

name: Professional rules for synthetic respondents (MRS, ESOMAR, AAPOR)
headline: Three bodies hold materially different instruments - MRS AI guidance (Apr 2025), ESOMAR's '20 Questions' buyer checklist plus the 2025 ICC/ESOMAR Code, and the AAPOR Code revised June 2026 requiring disclosure of AI sample generation and human oversight - none of which is a certification or audit, and vendor 'automation' claims ('60 seconds vs six weeks') are speed claims, not verified employment effects.
rows: Professional standards vs synthetic respondents (MRS / ESOMAR / AAPOR) and labour substitution
note: Standards denominator for any later vendor-disclosure judgement; none of it is on main.

name: NatSec100 defence-startup rosters 2023-2026
headline: All four annual top-100 lists were captured (the 2025 list was published only as images and hand-transcribed), giving 196 distinct companies of which 24 appear in every year; the 2026 edition newly requires a federal contract, 23 of the 2025 names still need a human identity call, and the original outside-supplied 'seed' claims mostly cited untraceable sources.
rows: NatSec100 startup rankings 2023-2026
NatSec100 follow-ons: 2025 identity-source custody and matched-outcome/non-selection pilot
note: Clean base list other defence trails depend on; the 26-route identity-evidence custody for the 23 unresolved names waits in open PR #2639.

name: SNAP work requirements: federal rules and a 50-state matrix
headline: All four steps of the 'deserving/undeserving' pattern appear in federal documents and a federal study of nine states found the time limit cut participation without observed employment gains; the state matrix (50 states x 9 fields) has 229 of 450 cells filled and 11-12 states complete, with 37 of 50 states reporting use of discretionary exemptions in FFY2024 and 13 reporting none.
rows: SNAP work-requirement rules: the federal picture
50-state SNAP implementation and rule history
SNAP fifty-state implementation matrix (RD-04) retired at 12 of 50 states
note: Genuine checkable public-record work but ~35 micro-steps per state; the owner retired the programme on 11 Aug 2026 with Oregon/Wisconsin captures in an expiring Actions artifact.

name: Federal civil-rights rollbacks 2025-26 and the checks that held
headline: Official texts document EO 11246 revoked and OFCCP stood down, an April 2025 order deprioritising disparate-impact enforcement, a March 2026 contractor clause with debarment exposure and sixteen inspectors general fired, paired with counter-examples where checks worked (the Supreme Court unanimously struck the 'background circumstances' rule in Ames v. Ohio; GAO sustained a FEMA bid protest).
rows: Federal civil-rights rollbacks 2025-26 vs checks that held
note: Primary documents with dates; conclusion is only 'partial mechanism present'. Held from the site under the politically loaded umbrella thesis - publish on its own terms or not at all.

name: Presidents' campaign money versus their own businesses
headline: Every FEC spending file for 2004-2024 (588,535 payment lines across 37 presidential committees) was matched against 5,945 holdings rows read from 26 official Trump and Biden disclosures, giving 1,172 name pairs but 0 confirmed same-company matches (995 could not be dated); a USAspending search for 6 registry-matched Trump companies and 4 properties found 0 contracts.
rows: Presidents' campaign money paid to their own businesses
Presidents' financial disclosure documents (OGE and National Archives)
Trump business entities in the New York registry and the 2016 disclosure
Federal contracts paid to president-owned properties
Eight presidents, five conflict-of-interest tests
SEC name-match check for disclosure and campaign names
Presidents' business entities in New York records
note: A source-limited zero, not an exoneration: disclosures carry no holding dates and the method misses card spending and protective-detail lodging. The eight-president design is neutral but only Trump/Biden ran; the repo's own rules block publication pending an independent review.

name: Expert contradicts boss, expert removed: a neutral search
headline: Searching oversight records without starting from famous names (nine templates, ~300 hits, 65 kept) found the pattern at up to 6 of 7 steps in the Challenger launch decision, East River helicopter warnings, the SickKids/Apotex trial dispute and an INS official's testimony, while control cases show appeals, stays and regulators often did work, so the pattern is real in famous safety cases but not shown to be general.
rows: Epistemic ceiling (K0) part 2: neutral search for the same pattern
note: Best-run piece of the theory work; strongest hits are decades-old non-political cases and no reviewer has signed off.

name: Ukraine's Brave1 and battlefield feedback into allied procurement
headline: A Palantir-backed Brave1 combat-data platform onboards outside developers, and public routes trace Ukrainian frontline data into UK production orders, Polish drone methods and NATO architecture; Palantir's role outside the data room is unproven and the claim an operator can abort an interceptor rests on a first-party statement.
rows: Ukraine's Brave1 and battlefield-feedback transfer
note: Many Ukrainian MoD sources; no failed-test, casualty or compensation record.

name: Defence capital 'routers' across funds and government
headline: From 100 fund partners and advisers (30 LinkedIn captures) 17 people met a 3-of-8 'routing' threshold led by Silent Ventures' Jackson Moses (6/8), then Heidi Shyu, Trae Stephens, Katherine Boyle and Joshua Baer; the map is self-labelled partial with 9 of 17 leads never searched and the per-person trails are on the public list.
rows: Defense 'routers': people who sit across funds, advisers and government
Early defense seed queue and roster-scan template
note: The most distinctive investigative output in the defence work: Anduril sits in 8 of 11 funds, and Firefly's $113.5M ceiling compares with $76.6M paid. Self-labelled partial; 9 of 17 leads were never searched.

name: Dialog society directory names
headline: The ~115-person member directory of the Thiel-co-founded Dialog society, exposed by a website misconfiguration, was first turned into 6,579 pairwise links and then correctly reduced to a listing with zero links; Clifford told WIRED he was invited but did not attend, so the list links him to no one.
rows: Dialog leak: does appearing on the member list connect anyone?
Dialog estate (Thiel-linked society directory + UK AI policy)
note: A clean negative, and the 6,579-link mistake that produced most of the project's later safeguards.

name: Epistemic ceiling: the original named cases
headline: Thirteen events involving Musk, Bezos, Hegseth, RFK Jr., Zuckerberg, Rufo, DeSantis, Dean and Soon-Shiong were source-checked: six are well documented step by step (e.g. Musk firing the engineer who corrected him; the LA Times endorsement veto; New College tenure denials) and seven are not, with the RFK Jr. and both Hegseth chains falling to zero.
rows: Epistemic ceiling (K0) part 1: do the owner's ten named cases hold up?
note: Honest downgrades: the RFK Jr. and both Hegseth chains fell to zero. Pairs with the neutral-search version in this tier.

name: Estates and game trails: the attention map
headline: Twenty-four domains of attention (UK and US defence, local development, Dialog, offshore ownership, executive appointments, political finance, public money, regulatory markets, venture control, and ten frontier estates), each with its source families and denominator rules; the trail corpus holds 155 source-route runs and 94 custody runs across them, with 66 bounded non-overlaps, 5 exact pairs and 2 unresolved.

Venture capital and corporate-control estate
Ten 'frontier' estates (courts, lobbying/consulting, nonprofits, universities, AI/compute, energy, sanctions/export, patents, immigration/labor, property title/debt)
M-01 estate pass (143 tasks across 14 estates)
Game trails: what the 308 'trails' actually are
note: Fourteen estates had evidence before the structure was built; the ten frontier estates were surveyed with no records yet. This is the research agenda, not bookkeeping.

name: Official-record crawler
headline: Five scheduled adapters kept 35 records over two months (27 distinct US awards: 21 Palantir, 10 Anduril, ~$600M obligated) and rejected 1,741 hits including 1,664 from GOV.UK, so the UK side found nothing; 93 open triage issues hold the rejections.

Held crawler rejections and accepted-intake candidates (93 open packets, ~1,770 items)

name: Evidence lake, waves 1 to 20: identity and index layer
headline: Indexed every evidence file in the repo (1,277 with an owner), migrated all 176 entities and 164 claims onto the AXM Genesis ID scheme with zero change to evidence or hops, ran a cross-case identity census (229 distinct mentions: 121 canonical, 104 names not yet in the registry), made 57 adjudications, grew the canonical registry to 161 actors and 65 organisations (main has 32), and adjudicated 25,994 machine identifiers into a 10,612-record topology.
rows: Evidence-lake indexing and AXM Genesis identity-resolution waves 1-20
WebsiteIQ baseline audit and root 'Evidence Desk' publication estate
Pre-1.1 Atlas/aperture archive snapshots and the 1.4 placeholder
note: Bulk-closed 11 Aug 2026; only the ID scheme reached main (PR #2604). The 33 organisations only on the branch include Founders Fund, Detachment 201, Anduril PAC, SpaceX, Saudi PIF, the Federalist Society and HM Treasury. Exported into retrospective/2026-10-12/branches/.

name: POOF: the publication layer
headline: Built and on main since 30 Jul 2026 (PR #410): a generated review site with eight routes (report, reader file, examination, estate, newsroom, methods, machine, audit), five transaction schemas, a right-of-reply and correction record, and a validator that checks constitutional changes against the merge base; it is exercised in every release check and bound into stable-ground checkpoints SG-03 to SG-12.
rows: POOF and Clifford: turning a private manuscript into a public, challengeable publication system
note: This is the layer that lets the ledger stay neutral while an argument is sequenced and challenged in the open. Not yet deployed to a public address, and no cold reader has used it.

name: The constitution and the plan to 2037
headline: The one document in the owner's own voice (6 Jul 2026): eleven never-change rules (a source for every link, a shared record is not a relationship, no aggregation on ethnicity or national origin) and a five-phase plan to 2037 of which Phase 0 is closed.
rows: Build instructions: the rules and the plan through 2037
note: Rules 1.6 and 1.9 have no mechanical gate yet.

name: Allocator war, waves 21 to 38: the 2025-26 reallocation of selector authority
headline: Acquired 150 official-source files (8.5 MB) from the Federal Register, White House, DOJ, GAO, OPM, USAspending, the Supreme Court, MSPB and district courts: executive orders 14151 and 14173, the OPM DEIA-office RIF guidance, the OFCCP stand-down, the FAR overhaul, DOJ's Civil Rights Fraud Initiative with the IBM $17M and PayPal $30M settlements, the Title VI disparate-impact rule, the university agreements and investigations, Thakur v. Trump, AFGE v. Trump, Ames v. Ohio and the SBIC, OSC, Anduril DPA and Polar CHIPS awards; seven routes and 31 tasks, 28 holding official components and 3 protected.
rows: Evidence-lake indexing and AXM Genesis identity-resolution waves 1-20 (allocator-war part)
note: Zero completion tests pass because each demands a complete institutional row (the full agency implementation file, the full action register, realised payment recovery) that is not public. This is the raw material under the civil-rights-rollback finding. Exported into retrospective/2026-10-12/branches/.

name: Does a NatSec100 ranking cause contracts?
headline: Of 102 ranked names only 48 could be tied to a legal entity (44 ambiguous, 10 unreachable), and because the ranker never publishes the candidate pool or rejections there is no comparison group, so the question cannot be answered from public data.
rows: NatSec100: does the startup ranking pick winners?
Does making the NatSec100 list lead to government money?
